newsitem.title: PERU: Peru seeks $8 bln private investment for projects.
newsitem.headline: Peru seeks $8 bln private investment for projects.

text.p: The Peruvian government hopes to attract $8 billion in new investment by granting concessions to private businesses to carry out public infrastuctural projects, Presidency Minister Daniel Hokama said Friday.
"The 10 or so state projects we have along the coast require an investment of $12 billion, but the government has only invested $4 billion," Hokama told Reuters.
"Through the concession of these projects, we hope for an $8 billion investment from private firms, particularly foreign ones," he said.
In principle, the program, known as the "second wave of privatizations," would entail private companies gaining ownership of assets they construct or administer.
During that period, the company would have the right to charge the public for the use of the asset, Hokama said.
"The government's philosophy is: If the treasury does not have the money, we have to look for private investment," Hokama said.
Since 1991, the government took in $6.7 billion from the sale of state assets, according to the Peruvian privatization board (COPRI). It also received commitments from buyers to invest $4.85 billion.
The projects, which have already attracted the interest of 12 "very important foreign firms," involve the construction of hydroelectric centers, highways and the improvement of ports, Hokama said.
In December, the government will set up its first privatization committee to begin the process of inviting bids for concessions, the minister said.
He did not say when the government hoped to achieve its goal of $8 million in new private investment commitments.
-- Saul Hudson, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
